title: Vladimir Lenin
summary: Born Vladimir Ilyich Ulyanov in Simbirsk in 1870, Lenin led the Bolshevik faction from 1903 and played a leading role in the October Revolution of 1917, in which the Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government. His government withdrew Russia from World War I, won the civil war and suppressed opponents in the Red Terror, in which tens of thousands were killed or interned. He headed the Soviet Union from its formation in 1922 until his death in January 1924, and became an ideological figurehead of Marxism–Leninism.

uncertainty.note: Birth date 22 April 1870 in the Gregorian calendar, 10 April 1870 in the Julian (Old Style) calendar then used in Russia.

where.modern_name: Moscow, Russia (city point; Lenin's tomb is in Red Square; birthplace: Ulyanovsk, formerly Simbirsk)

importance.justification: Lenin played a leading role in the October Revolution and was the first head of government of Soviet Russia and of the Soviet Union, the world's first communist state. He is widely considered one of the most significant and influential figures of the 20th century.

audience_note: This record mentions political killings and internment during the Red Terror; estimates of the toll vary between sources.
